subject: Migration & deployment mode follow-up — Lumina Labs
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@luminalabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@luminalabs.com>, Procurement <procurement@luminalabs.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Thanks for the demo — quick follow-up on deployment modes

Hi Marissa and team,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the latency numbers look promising. Wanted to capture our current thinking so we can align on next steps. High-level context: Lumina Labs is evaluating moving production inference from an in-house GPU cluster + managed API gateway to a vendor-managed solution. Our top priorities are data residency, predictable throughput for peak trading hours, and tight SLOs on tail latency.

Questions we had after the demo:
- Hosted API: curious about isolation and data retention policies (we handle regulated customer data in US-only regions).
- Dedicated: what's the minimum committed capacity and what burst options look like for daily peaks?
- Private (VPC/on-prem): potential interest if we need full control over keys and audit logs — budget permitting.

We'd also like to understand migration support — specifically: do you help with model conversion/quantization and moving model artifacts from our legacy cluster?

Can we do a technical follow-up (30–45m) with your infra/solutions engineer next week? CC'ing Sanjay from our infra team.

Best,
Alex
VP Product, Lumina Labs
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@luminalabs.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — quick follow-up on deployment modes

Hi Alex — great talking earlier. Appreciate the clear priorities. Short answers inline, and proposed next steps below.

Inline:
- Hosted API: we can provide US-only region routing, strict retention settings, and SOC2/audit logging. For regulated PII we recommend Dedicated or Private but many customers successfully start on Hosted with encryption-at-rest and VPC peering options.
- Dedicated: minimum commit typically starts at monthly reserved GPU pods (we'll propose exact sizing after we see QPS/peak concurrency). Burst is supported through autoscaling pools; we can guarantee baseline throughput and configure burst buffers.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full audit logs, KMS/HSM integrations, and air-gapped options. Higher ops overhead but aligns with strict compliance needs.

Migration support: yes — our migration team helps with model conversion (quantization, kernel tuning) and artifact transfer. For legacy clusters we do a short discovery: model formats, tokenization, and a test export to validate perf.

Next steps:
1) Tech discovery call w/ your infra + our SE: propose Tue 17th 10:00am PT or Wed 18th 2:00pm PT.
2) I'll share a short deployment-options PDF and a draft mutual action plan (attached).
3) If procurement wants, we can include an indicative pricing range for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private in the MAP.

Attaching: deployment-options.pdf (short compare matrix).

–Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@luminalabs.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: technical notes & migration checklist

Hi Alex — following up with a concise tech checklist so we can scope the migration work. See below and the attached MVP-MAP-Lumina-2026-02.pdf for a proposed timeline.

Key items we need from Lumina:
- Current model formats (PyTorch, ONNX) and sizes (GB)
- Tokenizer details and custom pre/post-processing
- Typical batch sizes, peak QPS, and average request sizes (tokens)
- Current auth & key management approach (KMS/HSM)

Migration steps we offer:
1) Export & smoke test on a staging node
2) Quantization/format conversion + perf tuning
3) Canary run (Dedicated pool) and compare latency/cost
4) Roll to production — options: Dedicated or Private based on compliance needs

If you can share model exports and a small sample of traffic (sanitized), we can run an initial perf estimate.

Rishi
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@luminalabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@luminalabs.com>, Procurement <procurement@luminalabs.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Migration & deployment mode follow-up — Lumina Labs

Thanks Marissa and Rishi — that checklist is helpful. Quick clarifications from our side:
- Compliance: most of our customer data must stay in US regions; SOC2 is required. We prefer Dedicated for predictable throughput, but if Private gives us stronger KMS control we may consider it.
- Commit: what is the typical minimum monthly commit for Dedicated? We need a ballpark for our finance team.
- Migration scope: we can provide sanitized model exports and a small traffic dump. We will need assistance with quantization — our infra team does not have an MLE dedicated to this.

Procurement is interested in an indicative pricing table (hosted/dedicated/private) and any standard enterprise discounts. Also, any references for customers who migrated from on-prem GPU clusters would be helpful.

Sanjay (cc) — can you join the technical discovery on Tue 17th or Wed 18th? We prefer Tue 17th morning.

—Alex
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@luminalabs.com>

- Week 4 (Roll): production cutover or discuss Private deployment if compliance requires KMS/HSM isolation.

Deliverables: deployment-options.pdf (attached), MAP draft (attached), indicative pricing table to follow after discovery.

Action items:

- Schedule: tech deep-dive Tue 17th 10:00am PT — calendar invite to follow.

If procurement wants a templated SOW or reference contacts who migrated from on-prem, we can include both in the PR package.
